issues.title: Persistent/stale USE-keyspace failures discard connections indefinitely, can drain pool…
issues.verdictReason: The new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm at connection_pool.rs:900 unconditionally decrements the counter and drops the connection with no immediate retry (unlike the sibling Connection-error arm, which retries immediately on the non-shard-aware port when requested_shard.is_some()); if USE keeps failing (e.g. dropped keyspace), the pool empties and update_shared_conns publishes Broken(UseKeyspaceError) at line 909, whereas main's old code admitted the connection anyway with only a warning. Refills do keep retrying via the run() loop's growing backoff (not literally 'no exit' as one tool claims), but there is a real regression in availability for a known failure mode compared to before.
issues.scopeReason: The Keyspace-error branch and its drop/backoff behavior are new code added by commit 7f48315d.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: Shard-aware-port keyspace failure has no immediate fallback retry / Keyspace-change race can drop a connection despite the new keyspace succeeding
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: Pool becomes permanently unrefillable after any failed USE keyspace
reportedAs.tob-rust-review: Persistent USE failure causes pool to permanently starve and end up Broken

reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/quillstone/anthropi: Previously a failed USE was logged but the connection still joined the pool; now every such connection is dropped and refilled with growing backoff and no exit, so a persistent USE failure empties the pool, publishes Broken(UseKeyspaceError), and fires ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost even for fully-qualified queries.
reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/quillstone/mattpoco: On error, the Connection branch retries immediately on the non-shard-aware port when requested_shard.is_some(), but the Keyspace branch just drops the connection and waits for backed-off refill, undocumented and asymmetric; also if current_keyspace changes while a stale USE is in flight and fails, the connection is dropped even though the new keyspace might have succeeded.
reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/quillstone/tob-diff: The refiller stores current_keyspace before the USE result is known and never reverts it on failure; a connection whose USE fails is now discarded instead of admitted with a warning, and repeated failures can leave the pool permanently Broken(UseKeyspaceError).
reportedAsByRun.fable-5-1-2026-09-29/quillstone/tob-rust: Every newly opened connection is dropped in the new Keyspace error branch, backoff grows, and once existing connections die the pool ends in Broken(UseKeyspaceError) with no recovery except another successful use_keyspace call.

But because a connection stuck in the Keyspace-error branch never reaches the reshard code, a pool whose current_keyspace is set from creation and whose USE persistently fails will never learn the node's sharder or shard-aware port either.

issues.title: New ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant's semantics/#[from] are debatable
issues.verdictReason: ConnectionError is documented as meaning 'connection can no longer be used and should be dropped' (errors.rs:569-570), which doesn't strictly apply to a keyspace-not-found failure on an otherwise healthy TCP connection. The #[from] also auto-derives a public impl From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError even though UseKeyspaceError is also Session::use_keyspace's unrelated return type; only one in-crate call site (connection_pool.rs:909, via .into()) uses it. Minor and defensible either way, but a legitimate nit.
issues.scopeReason: The variant is new in this PR (errors.rs diff).

issues.title: Commit subject 'avoid busy-waiting' is claimed to overstate a fix that still polls
issues.verdictReason: Commit 617139df does replace `tokio::task::yield_now().await` with `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await` in the poll loop. Busy-waiting specifically refers to a hot spin loop that doesn't yield/sleep and burns CPU; replacing a yield_now spin with a sleep-based poll is the standard fix for exactly that, so the subject is accurate even though the loop still polls a condition.
issues.scopeReason: This is about this PR's own commit message.

issues.title: ConnectionSetupError lacks #[derive(Debug)]
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed: `enum ConnectionSetupError { Connection(ConnectionError), Keyspace(UseKeyspaceError) }` (line 1418) has no derive, unlike the neighboring ConnectivityChangeEvent which derives Debug just below it. Both payload types are Debug, so deriving it would let call sites use .expect()/.unwrap() instead of manual match+panic! (as the new test at ~1685-1689 does).

issues.title: OpenedConnectionEvent's keyspace_name/result coupling is unenforced by the type system
issues.verdictReason: OpenedConnectionEvent stores keyspace_name: Option<VerifiedKeyspaceName> alongside result: Result<..., ConnectionSetupError> as independent fields, so Err(Keyspace) with keyspace_name: None is representable though never produced in production code; the test at ~1495-1503 constructs exactly that combination. Moving keyspace_name into the success/Keyspace-error payloads would make the invalid state unrepresentable, but this is a minor type-design nit, not a functional bug.
issues.scopeReason: This struct is new/modified by this PR.
